label: text
text: The manouvres of two launches lying outside Bailey's shipyard in the early morning of September 8 aroused the suspicions of Mr. Edwards, an engineer in the employ of Messrs. W. S. Bailey and Co., and as a result of his observations four men appeared at the Criminal Sessions this morning, one charged with misappropriating coal and the others with aiding and abetting him.

label: text
text: The launches in question were the "Poseidor" and the "Tai Yuk Fong," the former being a Blue Funnel (Ocean Steamship Company) "launch" operating from Holt's wharf, and the latter the launch of Watson and Co., Ltd.

label: text
text: The coxswain of the "Poseido" was charged with misappropriating five tons of coal, at the Criminal Session, this morning, whilst the engineer and 2nd coxswain of the same launch, also the coxswain of the "Tai Yuk Fong," were charged with complicity.

label: text
text: The respective systems under which "the coxswains of the launches were engaged were referred to by Mr. G. K. Holmes, Crown Solicitor." The coxswain of the "Position" had coal supplied to him direct by his employers and the coxswain of the "Tai Yuk Fong" was paid $360 a month out of which he had to pay the crew and find the coal.

label: text
text: The "Posedon" coxswain had 12 tons of coal supplied him on September 6 at which time there was approximately 4 tons in the bunkers. Between that date and the morning of September 8, 2 or perhaps 10 tons, area liberal estimate might have been used, said the Crown.

label: text
text: At about 7 creek on the morning of September 8, Mr. Edwards noticed the two launched together lying outside Smiley's shipyard. Baskets were passing from the "Poseid" to "Tid" Yule Fong" when when he went to the water's water to see engine clear he not xing and xing. label: text
text:
The coxswain, and others on the "Poseidon" were arrested as a result of police investigation when the "Posedon" arrived at Holt's wharf, Mr. Fraser, of Bailey's, having been poned to Captain Griggs. The coxswain of Watson's launch was arrested later, the launch on investigation by the police having been found to contain her full coal capacity.
The case for the Crown proceeded no further than the outlining of the case at the Court this morning, the judge, Mr. Justice Wood, counsel, the Hon. Mr. C. G. Alabaster, K.C., (instructed by Mr. D. McCallum) and Mr. Elsley Zeillyn (instructed to defend Watson's coxswain by Mr. Remedios) all proceeding in the launches to the scene where the alleged misappropriation took place.

An excuse that he was going in search of an employee who abandoned with $1,600 belonging to a foundry at Yaumuti was tendered at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning when a Chinese was charged with attempling to export $15 from the Colony and thus contravening a strike emergency enactment which is still in force.
Sergeant Morton said he did not wish to press the charge as the defendant when arrested on the train yesterday had been quite straightforward and told the same story.
In answer to a question, defendant said that he did not intend to cross the border. Another object of his journey was to await the arrival of his wife, who was on the Chinese side.

label: text
text: The money was returned to the defendant and he was discharged with a caution.

text: Considered an indication that the Reds have advanced materially from their original base in the campaign against the Chan Kwing-ming party, is the announcement by the Chinese section that passengers will again be carried on that part of the Kowloon-Canton Railway from Canton to Simechon, as from tomorrow.

label: text
text: At the height of their success, General Chan's army reached positions from which they could strike at vulnerable points on the railway. Civil transport was interrupted by丙ontic moves on Canton's part to rush reinforcements to the front. With the fall of Wuchow the position—from Canton's point of view—has been eased.

label: text
text: Conflicting reports have been received regarding the fall of Waichow, the Chan stronghold on the East River. Some maintain that only the district capital by that name was surrendered to the Cube, but later reports claim that netted Cheging Kūi-shek's men are generally in the capital of the next seifure take of the same name as well.

Pakkai, Kongmoon, Oct. 8.
All firms here, with the exception of British, have resumed trade. The Marion Barclay Hospital (Caneolian) and schools are still closed.

label: text
text: The situation generally is normal. Business is dull. The harvest has been good.

label: text
text: H.M.S. "Mourhen" and H.M.'s armed launch "Kwong Lee" were here during the greater part of the strike.

label: text
text: There is a shortage of kerosine and' liquid fuel. Merchants have attempted to smuggle the commodity in but their junks have seldom got through the strike pickets' cordons.. All seized cargoes are confiscated.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Leung Kwong" (formerly on the Hongkong-Kong-moon run) is now plying between Canton and Wuchow. The s.s. "Kung On" was removed from Pakkai to Kong Mei, the owners' village, for fear of being "requisitioned" by strikers or the military.

label: text
text:
Some of the men of the former commander at this port (Li Yatngok who fled to Hongkong after the first Red coup) have turned pirates and established "themselves at Pa Chung. A combined force of village guards and Kongmoon (Kuomintar) soldiers attacked the outlaw and dislodged them. Three pirates were captured. On his following being disbanded, Li Yatngok retired to Yanping, joining Leung Hung-kai's remnants.
Pirates have again been active in the neighbourhood of this port. The Merchants' Volunteers (now known as the "Mai Tain") have authority to pay for the before the Saikwan Massacre of a year ago.
At present Commander Leung Hung-layn is brother of Leung Hung-kai, the alleged anti-Red general detained at Whampoa is at Chekhom and Yamping with his troops. General Li Chai-sum, the Red nominee, holds Sunning. Kungyick and Sanwui but he himself is absent from the sphere of operations. Kongmoon is in the hands of Brigadier-General Chan

label: text
text: Many junks have been commandeered to transport troops to Canton and communication with other river ports has been suspended for over a week but is now re-commencing.

label: text
text: During the present trooping season, there have been no pressgangs at work. Coolie volunteers are asked for. Even at $16 a month, there are very few coming forward. Accordingly the magistrate had ordered the prisoners on small offences to be put on to military transport.

label: text
text: The Commissioner of Police (Cheung Cho-wing) has been dismissed and Li Poon is in his place. The Commissioner of Customs is leaving for Home this month.

label: text
text: A Chinese who graduated in an American course of engineering has proposed establishing a waterworks at the top of Kwei Fung hill, outside Saiwui city. He is asking for subscriptions for shares and it is hoped that a modern supply of water will soon be available.

label: text
text: Saltfish is the only import permitted from Macao but boats are low running here from Shekki.

label: text
text: It transpires that a Portuguese watchman was killed in the "Kwok Ning" piracy (report) previously in the "China Mail").

label: text
text: Rice-mill workers are striking for higher pay. Negotiations have been going on and rice is a little higher. Premium on Hongkong banknotes (in exchange for Canton subsidiary silver coin) is 20 per cent.

label: text
text: The warship entering the harbour yesterday was H.M.H. "Waymouth" from Haine, bringing a relief from H.M.S. "Carliie" H.M.S. "Weymouth" will remain the barbour for a few

label: text
text: The action of the strike pickets in actually supervising the landing arrangements at Canton for passengers carried by the s.s. "Honam" on her last trip illustrates the general weakening of the strike directed against Hongkong. The prices charged by the junk and samparas operating under their supervision are considerable and it is doubtless their need of such revenue that has led to the change of front, but the fact remains that no difficulty was experienced by passengers desirous of landing.

label: text
text: The "Honam" left again this morning with 400 passengers, nearly all of whom were Chinese. The "Fatshan" will leave tomorrow. No arrangements have to be made by the Steamboat Company for the "special tugs" which were deemed necessary to navigate that portion of the river which the Canton Government has stated is mined; what actually occurs is that the signal to stop is given from the hillside off Bocca Tigris forts, whereupon a boat puts out, questions about cargo and passengers carried are asked and a pilot boat proceeds ahead, deviating but slightly from the usual route.

label: text
text: The strikers' executive have acquired considerable power in the absence of troops in the neighbourhood of the East River. The seizure of Annamite clerks in the employ of the Banque de l'Indo Chine is typical of their high-handed actions. These clerks had spiked through the French gate and presumably had the passes from the French Consul without which they are not allowed to pass through into Cantor.

label: text
text: The disarming of the strikers upon the return of the troops from Whichow is looked upon as a certainty, as the Canton authorities are stated to have regarded the strikers' growing power with considerable uneasiness. but they have been powerless as yet to act in the matter.

label: text
text: Application for the provisions of the Trade loan were asked to be made by Wednesday, October 22, but the “China Mail” understands that this date was not looked upon as final, the idea in fixing a day being to have indicated the measure of the demand.

label: text
text: Many applications have been made, some of which are not thought to come under the category of needy relief and will therefore have to stand down. The sums applied for do not amount in aggregate to anything like £3,000,000.

label: text
text: The credit placed with the Colony in this manner will, however, be kept for the purpose for which it was asked and firms wishing to avail themselves of a portion of it may make application at any time.

label: text
text: "N.E. winds, fresh; fair," is the weather forecast still noon tomorrow, for Hongkong. For the Formosa Channel it is "N.winds, fresh to strong". The museum will fresh along the coast and over the northern China Sea.

text: The local offices of the Asiatic Petroleum Company, in whose hands are arrangements for his landing, are in receipt of a cable announcing that Commander Di Pinedo, the Italian aviator, arrived at Amoy at 11:45 this morning. He anticipated leaving Amoy an hour later and making Hongkong between four and five o'clock today.

label: text
text: Tokyo, October 17.—The Italian airman Commander DI Pinedo hopped off for Kegoshima this morning.—Reuter.

label: text

Shanghai October 18.—Com-
mander Di Pinedo arrived here at 12.15 pm. from Japan — Reuter

label: text
text: 12.15 pm. from Japan.—Reuter. Other world aviators have accomplished the journey from Hongkong to Amoy by air (roughly from 350 to 400 miles) in about five hours. Commander Pinedo's machine is similar to that of Major Maclaren, the British world fiber, and is of the heavy flying boat type. The excellent flying time he has made since he left Japan speaks well for the new engine he had fitted there.

label: text
text: Commander Pinedo set out from Sesto Celende, near Rome, on April 22, his object being to fly to Tokyo via Australia and the Philippines and to return by the route followed by other fliers.

text: Lord D'Abernon, the British Ambassador, in a-greeting to the German Delegation on their return from Locarno, congratulated them on behalf of Mr. Austen Chamberlain who would always remember their spirit of sincerity and frankness, and added that the honour in taking the initial course of action resulting in the Treaty belonged to the German Government.

label: text
text: The Locarno agreements mark a turning point in the history of Europe.

label: text
text: In a speech at the closing banquet of the Radical Congress, M. Painleve, the Premier, declared the Locarno agreement were the outcome of Carle's policy and inaugurated a new era.

label: text
text: At the conclusion of the Radical Congress, Mr. Painlevo promised that he and Mr. Herrick would discuss the most efficacious means of dealing with the formidable difficulties confronting the country.

label: text
text: He pointed to Locarno as evidence of the Castel's policy of international peace and added that all danger in Morocco was now past. France desired neither consquent nor oppression, and was only less doing for peace.
